minimal_change_policy.peer_semantics: New write_half_close command accepts only completed sole /health response with no pending body. After flushing protocol output, base socket.socket.shutdown(SHUT_WR) ends only write side. It does not set eof/stopping/failed or close socket, emit physical events, alter counters/caps/deadlines, join prematurely, or swallow syscall errors. minimal_change_policy.tls_reason: Pinned CPython3.13.15 ssl.py:1340–1343 SSLSocket.shutdown clears _sslobj before invoking base shutdown. Calling socket.socket.shutdown on the actual SSLSocket deliberately uses the base public socket syscall and preserves its read decoder. Do not call client["socket"].shutdown(...) or use full close plus synthetic EOF.
minimal_change_policy.tls_limit: SHUT_WR is an explicit TCP write-half-close, not a claimed graceful TLS close_notify exchange. Actual remote EOF/reset remains mandatory and observable; no network outcome is inferred from command ack.
